surfaces.part: magic circle disc (grey outer ring, blue rune rings, glowing center)

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a near-perfect circle, 48 px wide at its widest (rows 22-25) and 48 rows tall. The width profile is symmetric top to bottom (4,14,20,24... up to 48, then back down to 4), so the disc is not foreshortened. There is no front (south) face, no thickness band, no front-edge line and no eave shadow. The grey ring is only an outline and the rune rings are drawn as concentric patterns seen straight from above. This is a flat decal drawn top-down with no front face, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 10 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference. Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans dark navy or blue-grey, a dark tone of the adjacent material rather than a black sticker line. The rune ring and glowing core step through about 5 blue lightness levels, and the stone disc shows a slate gradient with ring bands and rune marks. It has only 14 distinct colours in total, so the texture is less grainy than the Beodeul grass or paving. That is acceptable under a locked palette, since the visible tone count is at or above the references. Overall it reads as a crafted ground piece, not a flat sticker.
